messages:
jen (Support): FYI escalation from AcmeCorp (acct 7654). They report intermittent SSE disconnects and partial event payloads after page prefetch/navigation. Happening across Chrome and Safari, but much more visible in Safari when a service worker is present. Ticket: <https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/ACME-12345|ACME-12345>

jen (Support): Customer timeline: open page -> prefetch of app shell (link rel=prefetch) -> navigate -> EventSource connects -> stream starts -> after ~15-60s it either stops producing events or the client reconnects and receives overlapping/duplicate partial chunks. They see many reconnections in short succession.

eve (Customer): adding more detail from our side: we tested with CloudFront in front of the origin. When CloudFront has a cached SSE response (max-age set by our origin), reconnects sometimes get a 200 cached response that is truncated mid-stream. Safari seemed to concat previous chunks on reconnect. We tried the eventsource-polyfill (https://github.com/Yaffle/EventSource) to help on older browsers.

sam (Eng): thanks — a few initial hypotheses: 1) CDN caching of SSE endpoints (should be no-cache), 2) service worker/prefetch returning stored response not behaving like live stream, 3) polyfill differences for Last-Event-ID handling. Can you grab the original request ids and server logs around the failing times? Also confirm response headers for the SSE endpoint (Content-Type, Cache-Control, Transfer-Encoding).

jen (Support): customer sent headers and a small snippet of access logs. Pasted below (sanitized):

```
> GET /stream?sess=abc123 200 0.147  tx=rid-3f4a
> GET /stream?sess=abc123 200 0.002  tx=rid-3f4b (cached-from=edge)
> GET /stream?sess=abc123 200 0.000  tx=rid-3f4c (cached-from=edge)
> Response headers (first connection): Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300; Transfer-Encoding: chunked
> Response headers (cached hit): Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300; Age: 42
```

kai (Frontend): that matches a classic problem — browsers expect event-stream to be live; caching a chunked response lets edge return a snapshot that can be truncated. On reconnect the browser may re-use the lastEventId and the edge may replay a stored partial body. Safari's EventSource has some oddness with prefetch/service worker where the prefetch response is reused without establishing a proper streaming connection.

sam (Eng): agree. Immediate mitigation is to ensure SSE responses are not cached at the CDN. Server should set: `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, private` (or at least `no-cache, no-transform`). Also set `Surrogate-Control: no-store` for CDN layers. And ensure the CDN is configured to bypass cache for `Accept: text/event-stream` requests.

mark (SRE): repro steps I ran from staging to simulate CDN behavior:

```
# simulate client connecting and then a cached reconnect
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://staging.example.com/stream?sess=test" -N
# in another terminal simulate a cached edge response
curl -I "https://edge.example.com/stream?sess=test"
```
Output showed the edge returning `Age: 10` and the response body stopped after a partial event (ended mid-line).

kai (Frontend): frontend fallback: if you detect a service worker or prefetch in play, verify `navigator.serviceWorker` handlers don't intercept `/stream` requests. Service workers can accidentally return cached responses for streaming endpoints. Recommend adding `event.request.mode === 'navigate'` checks or explicitly bypassing your SW cache for `/stream`.

sam (Eng): another note about polyfills: some polyfills implement SSE over XHR/fetch and buffer differently, which can hide or amplify the problem. If the polyfill replays buffered chunks on reconnect without the same semantics as native EventSource `Last-Event-ID`, you'll see duplicates. Where possible prefer native EventSource and only polyfill fallback to fetch+readable-stream with clear dedupe logic.

jen (Support): proposed action items for customer: 1) Set `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate` and `Surrogate-Control: no-store` on SSE responses. 2) Add `Vary: Accept` (or include Accept in CDN cache key) so edge won't serve a cached HTML/other content for SSE requests. 3) Temporarily disable prefetching of the app shell for impacted routes or scope prefetch away from pages that will immediately open an SSE. 4) If using service workers, add a SW rule to `return fetch(event.request)` for `Accept: text/event-stream`.

sam (Eng): also ensure server sends an `id:` field regularly (heartbeat) so EventSource lastEventId is predictable, e.g. `:heartbeat\n` or `id: <timestamp>\n\n`. And make `Connection: keep-alive` explicit to avoid some edge timeouts.

jen (Support): I applied a staging change to set `Cache-Control` headers for `/stream` and asked CDN team to bypass cache for requests with `Accept: text/event-stream`.

deploy-bot: config-change 1947654330 deployed to staging by sam — changed `/stream` response headers (Cache-Control + Surrogate-Control)

mark (SRE): ran a staged repro after deploy — reconnects are now creating new origin connections instead of returning cached bodies. Curl now shows continued chunking and no truncated responses.

eve (Customer): we disabled CloudFront caching for `/stream` and scoped prefetch away from the page with the live stream. After a few hours we saw far fewer disconnects and no duplicated partial events. Thanks, will monitor. :thumbsup:

jen (Support): follow ups: 1) sam to push header change to prod and update CDN rules to bypass cache for Accept=text/event-stream, 2) kai to add SW-safe rule to our template and document in DEVs docs, 3) jen to send customer a summary and track in ACME-12345.

sam (Eng): I'll schedule prod rollout today and add a short note in the changelog. Also will add a quick npm snippet for clients who must fallback to `fetch` polyfill with dedupe guidance.

kai (Frontend): will add a sample SW snippet in devdocs:

```
self.addEventListener('fetch', event => {
  if (event.request.headers.get('Accept') === 'text/event-stream') {
    // don't cache or respond from SW for SSE
    event.respondWith(fetch(event.request));
  }
});
```

jen (Support): closing for now — reopen if customer sees recurrence after prod rollout. Thanks everyone.
